about: Press and interview parameters (OPUS-PEOPLE press, from OPUS-GOV's first version). Outlet counts and news habits live in data/research/press/local-news-2026.json.

maxOutletsPerKind.source: The outlets of one kind that cover the town's politics are kept to a handful; a big county's hundreds of radio stations mostly carry music, not local news.

newsRadioShare.source: Share of full-power radio stations airing news or news/talk formats (Pew State of the News Media audio fact sheets: about 10% of commercial stations air news/talk).

interviewsPerWeek.source: Candidate interviews one local outlet's political reporter can run in a week next to other assignments (local newsrooms average about 5 journalists per paper, data/research/press/local-news-2026.json staff).

invitationWeeks.source: Weeks before a general election in which local outlets seek out the candidates on the ballot (endorsement interviews and voter guides run in the final month or two).

televisionBar.source: How newsworthy a candidate must be for a television station to give airtime (name recognition, incumbency, money); newspapers and radio take any candidate on the ballot.

incumbentNewsworthiness.source: The newsworthiness an incumbent carries over a challenger (incumbents draw more coverage: Prior 2006, 'The Incumbent in the Living Room').

moneyNewsworthiness.source: Weight of a candidate's share of the money raised in the race on their newsworthiness.

questionsPerInterview.source: Questions on the record in a short candidate interview or questionnaire.

interviewWeight.source: How far one interview read or watched moves a person's view of the candidate, between an ad (secondhand, paid) and a speech heard in person.

brokenPromiseNewsWeight.source: How strongly a promise the candidate broke draws a reporter's question, against the other reasons to ask (accountability questions lead candidate interviews: Ballotpedia and League of Women Voters candidate questionnaires).

recordVoteNewsWeight.source: How strongly each of an incumbent's recent recorded votes draws a question about it (local coverage of officeholders centers on their votes: Arnold 2004, Congress, the Press, and Political Accountability).

recordVotesConsidered.source: How many of an incumbent's most recent recorded votes a reporter looks over before an interview.

partyGapNewsWeight.source: How strongly the distance between two candidates' positions on a question (0 to 2, halved) draws a question: reporters frame races by where the candidates differ (Patterson 1993, Out of Order).

townConcernNewsWeight.source: How strongly the town's own concern (the summed strength of its people's stances on a question over its adults, 0 to 1) draws a question; local outlets cover what their audience cares about (Hamilton 2004, All the News That's Fit to Sell).

divisiveNewsWeight.source: How strongly a question's national divisiveness (how partisan and how evenly split, 0 to about 1) draws a question beside the race's own record.

askedAgainPenalty.source: How much less a question draws each time this candidate has already answered it on the record: a reporter looks for what the candidate hasn't said yet.

interviewShyness.source: A candidate declines a reporter only when shy and averse to conflict and risk together (sociability plus half of conflict and risk below this).

reportersPerNewspaper.source: Reporters a local newspaper puts on one town's government (Medill State of Local News 2024: about 5 journalists per surviving paper across all its beats and towns; a small-town paper has one on its government).

reportersPerStation.source: Reporters a television or news radio station assigns to one town (a station covers a whole market; Pew local TV fact sheet 2023, RTDNA newsroom survey 2024: median local TV newsroom about 40 staff across a market of dozens of towns).

reporterAgeMin.source: Youngest working reporters, out of college (BLS CPS 2023 age of news analysts, reporters and journalists: median 38).

reporterAgeMax.source: Oldest working reporters (BLS CPS 2023: few reporters past their early sixties).

editorAgeMin.source: Youngest editors and publishers of a local outlet (BLS CPS 2023 editors: median age 44).

editorAgeMax.source: Oldest editors and publishers still running a local paper (owner-publishers often work past 65).

reporterAnnualPayMinor.source: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2023, 27-3023 News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists: median annual wage $57,500.

editorAnnualPayMinor.source: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2023, 27-3041 Editors: median annual wage $75,020.

fullTimeHoursPerYear.source: Full-time year used by BLS to turn an hourly wage into an annual one (40 hours times 52 weeks).

newspaperRevenuePerFollowerYear.source: A local paper's subscription and advertising revenue per reader per year (Pew State of the News Media 2023: about $20 billion of newspaper revenue against roughly 20 million weekday print and digital subscribers, about $1,000 per subscriber across a household's readers; a small-town paper earns far less, so about $150 per adult reader).

televisionRevenuePerFollowerYear.source: A local television station's revenue per adult viewer in one town, for the town's share of its newsroom (Pew local TV fact sheet 2023: about $18 billion of local station advertising across roughly 250 million adults, about $70 per adult, of which the news share is about $60).

radioRevenuePerFollowerYear.source: A news radio station's revenue per adult listener in one town (Pew audio fact sheet 2023: about $10 billion of local radio advertising across about 230 million weekly listeners; news and talk stations' share, about $30 per listener).

storiesPerReporterWeek.source: Government and politics stories a local reporter files in a week beside other assignments (Pew 2019 study of local news: local outlets run about 0.6 civic stories a day across their staff, about two a week per reporter covering a town).

storyProximityTown.source: How much a local outlet values a story from its own town, the scale the other proximity weights are set on.

storyProximityCounty.source: Weight of a county story at a town outlet against a town story (local outlets lead with their own town; Pew 2019).

storyProximityState.source: Weight of a state story at a town outlet against a town story (statehouse coverage fell by a third from 2003 to 2014; Pew 2014).

storyProximityNation.source: Weight of a national story at a town outlet, which leaves national news to the wire and networks.

storyReaderCareWeight.source: Weight of how strongly the outlet's followers hold views on a story's topic in what the reporter picks (outlets cover what their audience follows: Gentzkow and Shapiro 2010).

storyPeopleWeight.source: Weight of how many of the outlet's followers the story names or involves (news values of proximity and human interest: Galtung and Ruge 1965).

storyDriveWeight.source: Weight of the reporter's own causes and grudges in what they pick.

storyFreshDays.source: Days a public record stays a story a reporter can still pick (news ages out within a week or two).

slantLeanWeight.source: How far the outlet's lean tilts a story for or against its subject (media slant follows audience lean: Gentzkow and Shapiro 2010).

slantTieWeight.source: How far a reporter's closeness to the subject softens a story, and a grudge sharpens it.

slantPublisherWeight.source: How far the publisher's closeness to the subject softens a story (owner influence on coverage: Martin and McCrain 2019).

slantAdvertiserWeight.source: How far a subject's ad spending at the outlet this cycle softens its stories, at its full share of the outlet's year (advertiser influence on local coverage: Reuter and Zitzewitz 2006).

storyImpulse.source: How far one printed story moves a reader's stance on its topic, against a speech heard in person (1).

digDelayDays.source: Days a reporter takes to check a candidate's claim against the record before printing what they found.

moveWeightPlain.source: How far a plain answer carries in print, the scale the other moves are set on.

moveWeightFurther.source: How far an answer backed with a fact from the record carries in print against a plain one.

moveWeightTurn.source: How far an answer turned back on a rival carries for the candidate's own position (the story is partly about the rival).

moveWeightBrief.source: How far a brief answer carries in print against a plain one.

outletLeanHeadWeight.source: Share of an outlet's lean set by its head's own views; the rest follows its audience (Gentzkow and Shapiro 2010: slant tracks readers' lean far more than owners'; Martin and McCrain 2019: a new owner moved local TV coverage right).

coworkerHoursAtOpening.source: Hours an outlet's staff have spent together by the opening, a week of shared work, so coworkers know one another.

bureauMarginShare.source: An outlet's operating margin over its town staff's pay where its wider area funds the town bureau (newspaper operating margins of about 5 to 10 percent: Pew State of the News Media 2023; local TV margins higher).

daysPerYear.source: Mean days in a Gregorian year (365 plus a leap day every fourth year, less three per 400 years: 365.2425; 365.25 as the calendar's working mean).

interviewHours.source: Hours a reporter and a candidate spend together in a local interview.

contradictionWeight.source: How far a printed story setting a candidate's record against their word moves a reader's view of them, at the reporter's full resolve (fact-checks lower favorability of the checked politician: Nyhan and Reifler 2015; Wintersieck 2017).

distrustDistance.source: How far full distrust of an outlet moves a follower away from it, on the views lean scale (-2 to 2): at full distrust, as far as the scale's half-width (hostile media effect and outlet switching: Vallone, Ross and Lepper 1985; Stroud 2011).

ownerAgeMin.source: Youngest owners of a local outlet or station group (owners of U.S. newspapers and station groups are mostly past 50: Pew 2019 newspaper ownership study; Forbes 400 media owners).

ownerAgeMax.source: Oldest owners still holding an outlet (family owners commonly hold into their eighties).

outletLeanOwnerWeight.source: Share of an outlet's lean set by its owner's views (a new owner moved local TV coverage right: Martin and McCrain 2019; owners' influence on endorsements: Gentzkow and Shapiro 2010).

slantOwnerWeight.source: How far the owner's regard for the people a story names (closeness, a grudge, how near their views sit) turns its framing (Martin and McCrain 2019; Durante and Knight 2012 on owner-driven slant).

slantRivalWeight.source: How far the owner's regard for a candidate's rivals turns the candidate's own coverage the other way: an owner who crossed a rival favors the candidate.

regardViewsWeight.source: Weight of how near two people's leans sit in one's regard for the other, beside closeness and grudges.

tipDocumentsWeight.source: How far a paper trail (a payment on the books) pushes a reporter to dig into a tip, against a rumor with nothing to check.

exposureWeight.source: How far a printed story exposing an official's bribe moves a reader's view of them, at the outlet's full resolve (scandal coverage costs incumbents votes in proportion to exposure: Ferraz and Finan 2008; Snyder and Strömberg 2010).

nationalProximityTown.source: Weight of a town story at a national outlet against a national one (national outlets rarely cover one town's council).

nationalProximityCounty.source: Weight of a county story at a national outlet against a national one.

nationalProximityState.source: Weight of a state story at a national outlet against a national one (statehouse fights reach national news when they are national questions).

nationalProximityNation.source: Weight of a national story at a national outlet, the scale its other proximity weights are set on.

nationalInterviewBar.source: How newsworthy a candidate must be before a national outlet asks for an interview (name recognition, incumbency, money).

profileWeight.source: How far a magazine profile moves a reader's view of the person it profiles, at full framing (profiles shape name recognition and warmth more than a news item).

audienceRecountDays.source: Days between recounts of the town's counted residents for an outlet's audience and its stories' counted readers; audiences move by births, deaths and moves, which change a town's counts slowly within a month.

nationalStoriesPerReporterWeek.source: Stories a week a national outlet runs that bear on one town's state or the nation as its readers there follow it (a national outlet's few daily political stories are mostly about the capital and other states).

partyBreakNewsWeight.source: Weight on a question where a candidate's own recorded vote broke with their party's side, on the scale of a broken promise (reporters ask about party defections: Groeling 2010).

outletReadersNewsWeight.source: Weight on how far a candidate stands from the asking outlet's line on a question its readers care about (outlets ask what their audience cares about: Gentzkow and Shapiro 2010; hostile interviews probe weak points).

reporterCauseNewsWeight.source: Weight on a policy question the asking reporter holds a cause on, at full strength.

interestHeadWeight.source: How far an editor's regard for someone asking (closeness, a grudge, how near their views sit) weighs in whether the outlet gives them an interview, beside newsworthiness (editors' access relationships with sources: Gans 1979, Deciding What's News; same scale as the owner's slantOwnerWeight).

interestReadersWeight.source: Weight of the share of an outlet's followers who have heard of someone asking for an interview (outlets cover who their audience follows: Gentzkow and Shapiro 2010).

interviewAgainDays.source: Days before an outlet sits down again with an officeholder between races (a local beat reporter's monthly check-in with a council member or mayor).

officeNewsworthiness:president.source: Authority and reach of the serving office alongside personal recognition; Gans, Deciding What’s News (1979), prominence of national political leaders. This weight changes editorial scoring, not a guaranteed invitation.

officeNewsworthiness:vice-president.source: Authority and reach of the serving office alongside personal recognition; Gans, Deciding What’s News (1979), prominence of national political leaders. This weight changes editorial scoring, not a guaranteed invitation.

officeNewsworthiness:federal.source: Authority and reach of the serving office alongside personal recognition; Gans, Deciding What’s News (1979), prominence of national political leaders. This weight changes editorial scoring, not a guaranteed invitation.

officeNewsworthiness:state.source: Authority and reach of the serving office alongside personal recognition; Gans, Deciding What’s News (1979), prominence of national political leaders. This weight changes editorial scoring, not a guaranteed invitation.

officeNewsworthiness:county.source: Authority and reach of the serving office alongside personal recognition; Gans, Deciding What’s News (1979), prominence of national political leaders. This weight changes editorial scoring, not a guaranteed invitation.

officeNewsworthiness:city.source: Authority and reach of the serving office alongside personal recognition; Gans, Deciding What’s News (1979), prominence of national political leaders. This weight changes editorial scoring, not a guaranteed invitation.

officeNewsworthiness:township.source: Authority and reach of the serving office alongside personal recognition; Gans, Deciding What’s News (1979), prominence of national political leaders. This weight changes editorial scoring, not a guaranteed invitation.

storyRenownWeight.source: Weight of how many public figures a story names (a president, a governor, a member of Congress) in what a reporter picks: elite persons are a news value in their own right (Galtung and Ruge 1965, The Structure of Foreign News, Journal of Peace Research 2(1):64-91). Spread 0.5 to 2.

storyFriendWeight.source: How far a reporter's closeness to a person a story names weighs against filing it (reporters hold back or soften stories on friends and sources: Gans 1979, Deciding What's News; Sigal 1973 on reporter-source relations). A sliding term on the story's score, at most this share of its base.

storyLeakWeight.source: How far a reporter's closeness to the person who leaked a story to them raises its score (leaks flow along trusted source relationships: Sigal 1973; Hess 1984, The Government/Press Connection).

favorHours.source: Hours of time together the core's relationship writer records for a favor done for a reporter (a tip, an introduction, a quote on short notice), so closeness grows as with any contact.

leakHours.source: Hours of time together recorded when a source passes a reporter a leak.
